chapter: Breakup of Hines band to Lefty Bates
title: Fuller takes over the Grand Terrace and Fox's collapse
summary: Nine-piece Fuller band; Fox owed $600; club ended.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well, he had this big thing with Ed Fox. The Union got into it, law suits, what do you recall of that time? I presume he'd already broken up the band?
Yeah. Well, I was with Fuller then.
Fuller took the band into the Grand Terrace?
Yeah.
How many of Hines' band went with Fuller?
Well, most of the band. See, we didn't have a bigger band -- he didn't have as big a band as Earl had. I think we only had about nine pieces on that band.
Well, did Earl feel this was being disloyal to him?
No.
Because he'd already broken up --
He'd already broken up the band. And as we saw it, looked like he was really going into this cocktail thing, at the time, so we just went on with Walter Fuller.
Because the gig was there?
Yeah.
You needed the gig. But as you said, business was getting bad then.
Yeah.
And what was the reason -- business had been so good, and then business fell off. Was it just that the crowd had gone some place else?
The crowd had gone, I guess, some place else. I don't know why.
You know, the usual thing, clubs
get hot --
People just -- yeah, and then people just stopped spending the money. Had to -- getting along towards the end of the Depression, you know.
Yeah, and there was more money.
Yeah.
Well, according to news accounts of the time, that gig didn't last too long, did it?
No.
They closed at the end of 1940?
Uh-huh.
And he owed the band $600.00, according to this Downbeat story.
Yeah.
Did you ever get the money from Fox?
No.
What ever happened to Fox?
I don't remember. I don't know what he did after that. I think he got out of the band business.
Was that the end of the Grand Terrace?
Yeah, as far as Ed Fox was concerned.
Well, did somebody else --
Somebody else took it over, after a while reopened it. It was a little different set up, though.
You mean physically, or didn't have shows, or --
You didn't have shows, yeah. No band. Mostly jukebox.
Oh, really?
Uh-huh.
So that was really the end of the Grand Terrace?
Uh-huh.
Had the gangsters pulled out?
Oh, they'd been gone a long time before that.
So the money was gone?
Uh-huh.
(Recording interruption.)
